# R363 — Scratch alias real-reader boundaries and qualification gates

Date: 2026-10-13. Read-only audit of W `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-prefill-scratch-lifetime-alias-20261013`, source base `410904c`, concentrating on the new `STRATA_PREFILL_SCRATCH_ALIAS=1` path in `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`. I read the implementation and the scoped R356/R357/source-history reports. No source was changed and no build, test, import, AST, lint, GPU/profiler, process/service/reset, Git, or cleanup action was performed. The main official unchanged bench.sh COPY1 session remains outside this audit.

## Finding

I found no concrete stale reader, overlapping live range, missed alias count/carve, or out-of-order queue use in the source paths examined. That is a source-ordering result only; it does not establish alias parity or production qualification. The alias is guarded by a process-frozen exact `STRATA_PREFILL_SCRATCH_ALIAS=1` predicate used by both sizing and carve, and `Prefill::init` rejects a non-in-order compute queue before allocation. `Gemm::init_external` binds the same `m.cs` stream (`src/prefill/gemm.cpp:259-264`); every Gemm read/write relevant to these aliases is issued with that stream, so the in-order requirement supplies the needed ordering across kernel and Gemm submissions in source. It does not qualify any hidden backend queue behavior at runtime.

The `emb` lifetime is internally coherent across token and image cases. Batched native/quantized embedding gather and per-row/image upload all target `m.emb` on `m.cs`; when there is no `hand_in`, `gr_broadcast(m.emb, m.R, ...)` is its final reader before the layer loop. With `hand_in`, residual data goes directly to `R` and no embedding producer/reader is needed. `bo` aliases that same storage, but all its producers (GDN/QSA output or MoE combine) precede the corresponding `gr_write*` on `m.cs`. The first-layer write finishes before the layer-1 PLE upload can execute. Thus the initial embedding contents have been consumed before `bo` starts overwriting them.

`ple_emb` has two actual read paths: batched PLE GEMMs/post-ops at layer 1 and per-token `ple_block` at layer 1 (`prefill.cpp:1627-1665`). Both run on `m.cs`; their complete layer-1 work precedes the output write that reuses the plane as `bo`. The PLE host-to-device copy is queued on `m.cs` at `ple_land`, so the same queue orders the upload before PLE reads and after prior-layer writes. When PLE is off there is no upload/read. The stage branches are consistent with the same boundary: a stage ending before layer 1 lands after its final write; a stage beginning at layer 1 lands before its PLE read; later stages do not read PLE rows. Handoff copies `R`, not this plane, and the pre-existing handoff synchronization is retained. Image rows, BF16x2, MMQ/fallback, CPU expert output, and control-vector writes change producers or the selected `gr_write*`, but not this ordering boundary.

For GDN, qkv projection writes `m.qkv`; `gdn_conv` is its final reader and precedes `gdn_recurrence` on `m.cs`. With alias enabled, recurrence writes raw FP32 `y` at `m.qkv`; the normalizer still reads that raw y to form `y_h`, and output projection reads `y_h` into `bo` (the raw-y consumer must remain; see R350). `C >= ZV` is statically asserted and the two views start at the same base. The recurrences' serial, lane, D2, and key-head variants remain ordered by the same queue in the source call sequence. This source ordering does not substitute for variant-by-variant execution evidence.

Both alternative scratch layouts are freshly carved from the shared `m.region` base, with independent `Alloc` cursors for GDN, QSA, and MoE; they are not simultaneous live allocations. Actual region size is `max(gdn_set_bytes, qsa_set_bytes, moe_set_bytes)` and is likewise used by `bytes_needed`. The three omitted takes are omitted from both counting and carving under the same frozen predicate; no alias pointer is added to `owned`, and borrowed relayout syncs compute/copy streams before re-carving. The new trace reports addresses and candidate requested sizes after a successful carve, which can reveal address equality and selected max but cannot establish completion, bounds under device execution, or physical allocation size.

## Material behavior change and unresolved gate

The shared max is smaller for some T/mode combinations, and `draft_kv` and batched PLE derive their batch sizes from `m.region_bytes` (`prefill.cpp:976-1000, 1612-1626`). This changes their subbatching with no arithmetic change, so kernel source similarity alone cannot establish parity. In particular, the draft path returns `false` (falling back to the drafter's own pass) when the calculated aligned `B < 64`; this fallback boundary should be observed under alias ON and OFF. Batched PLE computes `SB=min(T, region_bytes/per_token)` and loops in SB pieces; runtime qualification should prove SB is positive for every supported production layout and compare all outputs/state. The source report R357's 8K/16K compact-fallback candidate winners (QSA at 8K, MoE at 16K) are useful expected-layout checks under exactly those assumptions, not evidence that the device path ran.

## Minimum executable gates for Main

1. In independent fresh processes, cover alias unset, `0`, exact `1`, and representative non-exact values (`01`, `1x`); verify frozen-at-first-reference behavior. For exact `1`, observe `emb==bo==ple_emb`, `qkv==y`, region bytes equal the selected candidate max, and matching `bytes_needed`/owned-carve and borrowed-carve accounting. Exercise small and tail T, borrowed relayout shrink/regrow, and verify the out-of-order queue is rejected before allocation. Check release/failure cleanup and that borrowed memory is never freed by the alias owner.
2. Run fixed-history comparator alias OFF versus ON with identical model/build/history/token IDs/offsets for the full required 32,049+ prompt and every chunk including tail. Compare logits/residuals and all persistent state relevant to continuation: GDN recurrent and convolution state, QSA KV codes/scales/indexer, PLE history; include save/restore plus second continuation and callback positions/counts. Keep the official out24 policy intact. Do not accept unchanged equations as the result.
3. Exercise real producer/reader combinations: token embedding and image rows; PLE batched, per-token, and disabled; layer split before layer 1, beginning at layer 1, and after it, plus `hand_in`; GDN serial/lane/D2/key-head branches and convolution short/tiled/norm branches; BF16x2, MMQ/mixed fallback, compact FP16 fallback, CPU expert share and control-vector writes. Include draft KV with batch enabled and the `<64` fallback edge, plus ring mode where supported. Compare behavior and state, not only successful completion.
4. In owned and borrowed modes, qualify allocation ownership, both direction relayout (smaller then larger), and queue completion/release on the exact production in-order queue. Verify no stale PLE upload or prior GDN qkv read remains when the overlapped write executes. Record effective modes/build/backend so results are attributable.
5. Only after those checks, run the normal official bench suite in Main's serialized window and record separate quality, memory, and performance results. Do not derive parity or fit from `STRATA_TRACE` addresses/counts or requested-byte arithmetic.

## Source trail

- Candidate `src/prefill/prefill.cpp:572-597, 677-684, 800-832, 899-936, 945-1005, 1320-1412, 1610-1666, 1688-1712, 2908-2965`: predicate, queue restriction, aliases, alternate-region counting/carving, relayout, embedding/PLE/GDN readers and writes, and region batch users.
- Candidate `src/prefill/gemm.cpp:259-264, 288-330`: external Gemm stream binding and stream passed through conversion/product submissions.
- R356 `research-prefill-16384-memory-actual-winner-round356-v1.txt`; R357 `research-prefill-lazy-gemm-and-alias-clipping-round357-v1.txt`; implementation note `implementation-prefill-scratch-lifetime-alias-v1.txt`; R350 raw-y consumer correction `research-gdn-y-kernel-consumer-alias-round350-v1.txt`.

No runtime proof is claimed. Main owns all executable qualification, measurement, and commits.
